subject: religious-studies
source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA A-Level Religious Studies specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: AS — two chosen options (one per area of study)
units.blurb: Choose two AS options from different areas of study

units.name: A2 — two chosen options (studied in depth)
units.blurb: Choose two A2 options from different areas of study

topics.name: AS 1: An Introduction to the Gospel of Luke
topics.blurb: Authorship, purpose and key themes of Luke's Gospel

topics.name: AS 2: An Introduction to the Acts of the Apostles
topics.blurb: The spread of the early Church from Jerusalem outward

topics.name: AS 3: An Introduction to Themes in the Old Testament
topics.blurb: Covenant, prophecy and key figures of the Old Testament

topics.name: AS 4: The Origins and Development of the Early Christian Church to AD 325
topics.blurb: Growth, persecution and consolidation of the Church to Nicaea

topics.name: AS 5: The Celtic Church in Ireland in the Fifth, Sixth and Seventh Centuries
topics.blurb: Origins, monasticism and missionary outreach of the Celtic Church

topics.name: AS 6: An Introduction to Islam
topics.blurb: Beliefs, practices and foundations of Islam

topics.name: AS 7: Foundations of Ethics with Special Reference to Issues in Medical Ethics
topics.blurb: Ethical theory applied to medical-ethics questions

topics.name: AS 8: An Introduction to the Philosophy of Religion
topics.blurb: Arguments for God, religious experience and evil

topics.name: A2 1: Themes in the Synoptic Gospels
topics.blurb: In-depth themes across Matthew, Mark and Luke

topics.name: A2 2: Themes in Selected Letters of St Paul
topics.blurb: Theology and themes in the Pauline epistles

topics.name: A2 3: Themes in the Old Testament
topics.blurb: Deeper study of Old Testament themes and texts

topics.name: A2 4: Themes in the Early Church and the Church Today
topics.blurb: Early-Church themes and their contemporary significance

topics.name: A2 5: Themes in the Celtic Church, Reformation and Post-Reformation
topics.blurb: Development of the Church from Celtic to post-Reformation eras

topics.name: A2 6: Islam in a Contemporary Context
topics.blurb: Islam and modern social, political and ethical issues

topics.name: A2 7: Global Ethics
topics.blurb: Applied ethical theory on global moral problems

topics.name: A2 8: Themes in the Philosophy of Religion
topics.blurb: Advanced themes in the philosophy of religion

connections.why: AS study of Luke is the foundation for the A2 in-depth study of the Synoptic Gospels
Acts narrates the very beginnings of the early Church studied historically in AS 4
Acts recounts Paul's missionary journeys behind the letters studied at A2
The expansion described in Acts develops into the early-Church themes examined at A2
AS coverage of the Church to AD 325 leads into the A2 study of the Church then and today
The AS introduction to Old Testament themes is deepened in the A2 option
The early Celtic Church studied at AS is traced through to the Reformation at A2
The Celtic Church grows out of the wider early Christian Church tradition
Foundational study of Islam underpins the A2 study of Islam in a contemporary context
Foundations of ethics at AS provide the theory applied to global ethics at A2
Introductory philosophy of religion prepares students for the A2 in-depth themes
Luke and Acts share a single author and form a continuous two-volume work
Ethics and philosophy of religion share the analytical and argumentative skills examined together
Philosophical reasoning about God and value underpins debates in global ethics
Old Testament covenant and prophecy form the background Luke draws on in his Gospel
Global ethical questions intersect with the contemporary social and ethical issues facing Islam
Gospel and Pauline material together build the A2 picture of New Testament theology
